model: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route)

historical_growth.fcf_cagr_basis: House (SBC-deducted) AFFO per diluted share: FY2020 $3.34, FY2022 $3.89, FY2025 $4.25. Reported AFFO per diluted share: FY2017 $3.06, FY2018 $3.19, FY2019 $3.32, FY2020 $3.39, FY2021 $3.59, FY2022 $3.92, FY2023 $4.00, FY2024 $4.19, FY2025 $4.28, 9M-2026 $3.35 (+5.0%), FY2026E $4.45-$4.46 (guidance raised Nov-2026, third raise of the year). AFFO available to common: FY2019 $1,050.0M, FY2020 $1,172.6M, FY2021 $1,488.8M, FY2022 $2,401.4M, FY2023 $2,774.9M, FY2024 $3,621.4M, FY2025 $3,885.9M. Dividends paid per share: FY2019 $2.7105, FY2020 $2.794, FY2021 $2.833, FY2022 $2.967, FY2023 $3.051, FY2024 $3.1255, FY2025 $3.217; current annualised $3.288 (monthly $0.2740, declared Nov-2026). Revenue, equity and EPS CAGRs are distorted by the VEREIT (Nov-2021, ~$17B) and Spirit (Jan-2024, ~$9B) all-stock mergers: total revenue tripled while AFFO per share compounded ~4%.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Judgment: 10-year house AFFO/share CAGR of the base path (FY2025 $4.25 -> FY2035E $5.77). Sits between the 3-year (+3.0%) and 5-year (+4.9%) per-share AFFO CAGRs; the 5-year figure carries the VEREIT merger accretion and the 2021-22 near-zero cost of capital, neither of which is a run-rate at a ~5% 10-year Treasury. Equity CAGR is not usable for a REIT (book equity is depreciated cost inflated by stock-funded mergers).
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (29.5% 5yr) and revenue CAGR (28.4% 5yr) diverge from EPS (0.3% 5yr) and per-share AFFO (4.9% 5yr) by far more than 30%. Expected: the VEREIT and Spirit mergers were paid in stock, so total revenue and book equity scale with the share count while per-share metrics do not. Growth was therefore selected from the AFFO/share series, not book equity or revenue.
historical_growth.notes: AFFO/share has grown every year since at least FY2017 but the rate has slowed from 4-6% (FY2018-FY2022) to 2-4% (FY2023-FY2026E) as the asset base passed $80B and the cost of capital rose. SBC is 0.5-0.7% of revenue (~$0.03-0.04/share), so house and street per-share values differ by under 1%. The dividend ($3.288 annualised) is 74% of FY26E AFFO; coverage is comfortable and retained AFFO (~$1.1B/yr) funds roughly a tenth of the investment programme.

scenario_narratives.base: Raised guidance ($4.45-4.46) delivered for FY2026, then per-share AFFO compounds ~3-3.5% as the industrial, data-centre and European pipelines plus 1.1-1.3% same-store growth outrun the refinancing drag and the dilution needed to fund ~$10B/yr of investment; the margin drifts 60bp lower as JV revenue consolidates. House AFFO/share compounds 3.1% over ten years, the dividend grows in step, and the exit multiple is 14x AFFO.
scenario_narratives.bull: Falling long rates restore a 150bp+ investment spread and a mid-teens-plus AFFO multiple, volume reaccelerates, and the Apollo/KKR/GIC/Cloud Capital fee platform adds a capital-light earnings stream, so per-share AFFO grows 4-5% for five years and the margin expands to 68.5%.
scenario_narratives.bear: Rates stay above 5%, the equity stays at 12-13x AFFO so external growth is throttled, debt re-prices 100-150bp higher, and a retail tenant credit cycle takes bad debt to 2-3% of revenue; per-share AFFO goes nowhere for three years and the stock is valued as a 1.5% grower at a sub-13x multiple. The A-rated balance sheet, 5.1-year maturities and 74% payout keep this a stagnation case, not a solvency one.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Realty Income is valued on the cash it actually distributes - AFFO available to common stockholders, after interest, NCI, recurring capex and (house basis) stock compensation - capitalised at a 9.5% USD cost of equity built off a ~5.1-5.2% 10-year Treasury, with net debt NOT deducted a second time. Three explicit ten-year per-share AFFO paths bracket the rate regime, the investment spread and tenant credit; the market price is read against where it sits between them. GAAP net income, EPS, P/E, EV/EBITDA and book equity are not used: ~$2.5B/yr of real-estate depreciation, stock-funded mergers and a >100% payout of GAAP earnings make them structurally uninformative for a net-lease REIT.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cost of equity: every 50bp on the 9.5% discount rate moves base value roughly 7-8%; a ~5.1% 10-year Treasury is high by post-2009 standards, so the valuation is richer if rates mean-revert and cheaper if they do not
Refinancing: ~$32B of debt at a 3.9% average coupon with 5.1 years average maturity re-prices toward 4.5-5.5%; each 100bp on the full stack is ~$320M (~7.5%) of AFFO once fully rolled

External-growth dependence: per-share growth above the ~1.2% same-store rate requires issuing equity at a multiple above the acquisition yield; at ~13x AFFO (7.6% yield) against a 6.8-7.2% initial cash yield the spread is thin to negative on equity alone, and the base path assumes it recovers

Tenant credit: top 20 clients are ~32% of rent; drugstore, dollar-store and casual-dining exposures have produced bankruptcies in 2024-2026 and the bear path carries 300-400bp of margin compression from bad debt

Share count: modelled flat with dilution netted inside the per-share growth path; 18.5M unsettled forward shares, two convertible note issues ($1.86B) and ~$10B/yr of equity-funded volume mean the absolute count will rise materially, so the paths must be read as per-share, not total-company, AFFO
New asset classes: $1.4B into the Cloud Capital hyperscale data-centre JV and European expansion carry underwriting and partner risk outside the retail net-lease core

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2025 total revenue (XBRL Revenues / 10-K). The engine's 'ebitda_margin_path' is the AFFO margin on this revenue line, not EBITDA: FY2025 AFFO available to common stockholders $3,885.9M = 67.6% of revenue (9M-2026: $3,140.8M on $4,718.0M = 66.6%; Q3-2026 65.4%). Growth is modelled PER SHARE against a flat share count: year 1 (+9.8%) bridges FY2025 AFFO to the FY2026 guidance midpoint ($4.455/share) on the September-2026 share count, i.e. it carries the accretion from shares already issued; from FY2027 the growth path is per-share AFFO growth NET of the ATM/forward dilution that funds the ~$10B/yr external investment programme. The model revenue line is therefore NOTIONAL: consolidated revenue is growing faster (9M-2026 +10.7%) at a lower reported AFFO margin, because the Core Plus Fund, Apollo JV and KKR JV are consolidated at 100% of revenue while AFFO is after their NCI share. Only the product (AFFO per share) is calibrated to guidance.
inputs.share_count_basis: 950.964M common shares at 30 September 2026 (Q3-2026 10-Q balance sheet; 950.997M on the cover at 28 October 2026) + 2.682M Realty Income L.P. common units convertible 1:1 (Q3-2026 10-Q NCI note) = 953.6M. AFFO is stated available to common stockholders after NCI, and the OP units share in it, so the divisor includes them. Held FLAT: SBC is charged through sbc_pct_path, and the 18.5M shares under unsettled ATM forward sale agreements (~$1.1B of expected net proceeds at a $58.97 weighted forward price, expected to settle by 30 December 2026) fund acquisitions not yet made, so their accretion and dilution both sit inside the per-share growth path, not the count. The $862.5M 3.50% 2029 and $1.0B 3.75% 2031 convertible notes carry capped calls and are not added to the count.
inputs.net_debt_note: Held at ZERO in the engine by design: AFFO is a post-interest flow capitalised at the cost of equity, so deducting the $31,369.5M net debt again would double-count it (ARG.NZ / PCT.NZ / IPL.NZ / SCG.AX / MAA / BXP treatment). Actual balance sheet at 30 September 2026 recorded in debt_memo.

debt_memo.net_debt_to_ebitdare_incl_forward_equity: Computed here: (31,369.5 - ~1,100) / 5,842.9 annualized pro forma adjusted EBITDAre; not read off the filing.
debt_memo.nci_note: NCI rose from $685M (Dec-25) to $2,385M (Jun-26) to $3,111M (Sep-26): U.S. Core Plus Fund $1,663M, Apollo JV $777M, KKR European JV $462M (formed Sep-2026), L.P. units $164M, other $44M. AFFO available to common already deducts the NCI share; unconsolidated JV debt is non-recourse and outside the consolidated figures (the company quotes $32.0B of pro-rata debt principal).
debt_memo.source: Q3-2026 10-Q (research/O/Extracted/O_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt): balance sheet, material-cash-requirements maturity table, net-debt / EBITDAre reconciliation, NCI roll-forward and ATM forward disclosure

inputs.fcf_definition: AFFO available to common stockholders, FY2025 = $3,885.9M (Normalized FFO $3,884.5M +/- debt non-cash items, leasing costs and recurring capex, straight-line rent, above/below-market lease amortisation, credit-loss allowance, SBC add-back; FY2025 10-K reconciliation). Already after interest expense, NCI, and recurring property capex. House (last_fcf) deducts the $30.77M 'amortization of share-based compensation' that Realty Income ADDS BACK into AFFO: 3,885.9 - 30.8 = 3,855.1. Development and acquisition spend is growth capital funded by retained AFFO (~27% after the dividend), debt and equity issuance; it is what the growth path pays for and is not deducted again.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K: cash-flow add-back $30,770k (XBRL ShareBasedCompensation) and the identical 'Amortization of share-based compensation' line added back inside the AFFO reconciliation. Unlike NAREIT FFO, Realty Income's AFFO adds SBC back, so the house basis deducts it once (sbc_pct_path); street basis = reported AFFO. 9M-2026 $27.1M (0.57% of revenue; run-rate ~$36M) against $21.7M in 9M-2025; the 0.65% path is left slightly above the run-rate.
inputs.buyback_note: 9M-2026 repurchases $290.6M (1.8M shares for $101.9M in January, 3.0M shares for $188.7M in August alongside the 2031 convertible; 10-Q cash-flow statement) under the $2.0B programme expiring Jan-2028 ($1.7B remaining) - the first buybacks in the company's history. Against ~$1.3B of forward-sale settlements (21.4M shares) in the same nine months the company remains a large net issuer; the flat count is a modelling convention (see share_count_basis), not a funded forecast.
inputs.horizon_note: FY0 is FY2025 actual; year 1 is FY2026 (guided, nine months reported and ten and a half elapsed at the valuation date), years 2-10 are FY2027-FY2035. Discounting the full FY2026 AFFO one year is conservative by most of a year's carry; the Jan-Nov 2026 monthly dividends have already been paid out of it. The FY0 roll to FY2026 belongs to the FY2026 10-K update, not this one.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity, not WACC, because the capitalised flow is post-interest. USD build: 10-year US Treasury + 0.85 beta x 5.0% equity risk premium. At the prior build (2026-10-01) the 10-year was 5.24% -> 9.5%. At this update it is 5.07% (Yahoo ^TNX, 2026-11-18), which builds to 9.3%. The rate is DELIBERATELY HELD at 9.5%: a 17bp move in the risk-free rate is inside a +/-25bp dead band, and re-marking the discount rate on every monthly wobble in the Treasury would make the valuation track the bond market rather than the business. It would be re-marked to 9.0-9.25% on a 10-year sustained below ~4.75%, and to 9.75%+ above ~5.5%; the sensitivity grid shows what each step is worth. The 5.0% ERP (vs 4.5% used for MAA) reflects O's higher leverage (5.4x net debt/EBITDAre vs 4.5x), ~$32B of debt at a 3.9% average coupon re-pricing toward 4.5-5% over 5.1 years, and a growth model that is wholly dependent on continuous equity and debt issuance (~$10B/yr). Cross-check: at the price in inputs.price_as_of the stock yields ~5.6% on the $3.288 annualised dividend and ~7.6% on FY26 guided AFFO, i.e. ~13x AFFO against a 2015-2025 range of roughly 13-21x; a 9.5% CoE with 2.25% terminal growth implies a 14.1x steady-state P/AFFO, the low end of that range. Single rate across scenarios; risk is carried in the paths and the probability weights, not stacked into per-scenario discount rates.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not applicable: Realty Income is the lessor under triple-net leases. Ground-lease rent it pays on behalf of clients (~$1.7B undiscounted over 50+ years) is reimbursed by those clients and is inside AFFO.
inputs.nci_treatment: AFFO available to common stockholders is after the NCI share of the consolidated U.S. Core Plus Fund, the Apollo JV, the KKR European JV and property partnerships ($3,110.7M book plus $71.7M redeemable at 30-Sep-26); 'AFFO allocable to dilutive noncontrolling interests' ($7.2M in 9M-2026) relates to the 2.7M OP units, which are included in the share count instead. No preferred stock outstanding.
inputs.notes: MODEL: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity, run through the Drivers/engine route with net debt held at zero (the GPT.AX/GMG.AX/CHC.AX/MAA pattern) - UNCHANGED from the 2026-10-02 build and matching the ticker's memory entry. Routed via .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md 'REIT / property trust' row: Realty Income is a self-managed US net-lease REIT; GAAP net income is dominated by ~$2.5B/yr of real-estate depreciation and lumpy gains/impairments, OCF less capex is not an owner-FCF series, and the sector is priced on P/AFFO and dividend yield. Engine mapping: revenue = notional revenue line compounding from FY2025 total revenue; ebitda_margin_path = street AFFO margin; sbc_pct_path = SBC/revenue (deducted for the house basis because O adds SBC back into AFFO); D&A, capex, tax and working-capital paths = 0 (recurring capex, leasing costs and TRS income tax are already inside AFFO). UPDATE 2026-11-19 (Q3-2026 10-Q, guidance raised 2 Nov 2026 to $4.45-$4.46). REFRESHED: price and timestamp; share count to 30-Sep-26 (948.9M -> 953.6M); balance-sheet memo to 30-Sep-26 (net debt $31.37B, 5.4x, unchanged ratio); buybacks ($290.6M 9M); forward equity (18.5M shares, ~$1.1B); dividend ($0.2740 monthly, $3.288 annualised, 137th increase). RE-JUDGED: year-1 growth only, in all three scenarios, so FY2026 AFFO/share lands on the raised guidance on the new count (base 9.0 -> 9.8 = $4.455 street; bull 9.2 -> 9.9 = $4.466; bear 8.5 -> 9.8 = $4.436, the bear's FY2026 shortfall narrowed from 4c to 2c below the midpoint because nine months are reported at $3.35 and one quarter remains). DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED, with what would move each: (1) FY2027-FY2035 per-share growth paths in all scenarios - Q3 gave no FY2027 guidance; 9M AFFO/share +5.0% and same-store rent +1.15% are in line with the base path; FY2027 guidance (February 2027) or an investment yield persistently below ~6.8% against an unchanged cost of capital would move them (Q3-2026's 6.8% initial yield, down from 7.2-7.3%, is one quarter and is flagged, not acted on). (2) AFFO margin paths - the reported consolidated margin fell to 65.4% in Q3 but that is NCI consolidation of the Fund/Apollo/KKR vehicles, not economics accruing to common; the model revenue line is notional (see base_revenue_note). (3) SBC path 0.65% - 9M run-rate 0.57%, left slightly conservative. (4) Cost of equity 9.5% - see wacc_rationale. (5) Terminal growth and cap multiples. (6) Weights 25/50/25 - the rate axis, leverage and tenant-credit picture are as they were; occupancy 98.8%, recapture 103.5%. The KKR JV, Mexico entry and Cloud Capital first closing are consistent with the base narrative (private capital substituting for public equity) and with fee income sitting in the bull path only. US-GAAP XBRL does not tag total debt or AFFO; both are read from the 10-Q MD&A tables.

bear.narrative: Higher-for-longer (10-year above 5%) keeps the equity at a 12-13x AFFO multiple, so the ~$10B programme shrinks to $4-6B/yr and is barely accretive; $3B/yr of 3.9%-coupon debt rolls at 5-5.5%; and a 2027-28 tenant credit cycle (drugstores, dollar stores, casual dining - top 20 clients are 32% of rent) pushes bad debt to 2-3% of revenue with 300-400bp of margin compression by FY2030. Per-share AFFO growth stalls at 0.5% for two years and recovers only to 1.5-2%; the dividend (74% payout) stays covered so this is a growth problem, not a distribution cut. Terminal 1.5% with a 14x cap (Gordon at 9.5%/1.5% is 12.7x, so Gordon binds).

base.growth_note: Year 1 is the bridge from FY2025 AFFO ($3,885.9M street) to the FY2026 guidance midpoint ($4.455 x 953.6M = $4,248M) on the September-2026 share count; FY2027-FY2035 are per-share AFFO growth rates against a flat count and are UNCHANGED from the 2026-10-02 build (same-store rent +1.1-1.3%, plus ~2-2.5% of spread-investing accretion at a ~7% initial cash yield against a ~6.5-7% blended cost of capital, fading as the base compounds).
base.ebitda_margin_note: Street AFFO margin on consolidated revenue. FY2025 67.6%, H1-2026 67.2%, 9M-2026 66.6% reported (the consolidated Fund/Apollo/KKR revenue carries an NCI deduction; the model revenue line is notional and the path is calibrated so that AFFO per share ties to guidance). Drifts to 67.0% as consolidated JV revenue grows and ~$31B of 3.9%-coupon debt rolls toward 4.5-5% (each 100bp on $3B/yr of maturities is ~$30M, ~0.5pt of margin), partly offset by rent recapture above 100% and the capital-light fee stream.
base.narrative: FY2026 lands at the guidance raised in November ($4.45-4.46 AFFO, ~$10B invested at ~7.1%), then per-share AFFO compounds ~3.5% for three years as the Cloud Capital data-centre JV, GIC industrial build-to-suits and the European book deliver, fading to 2.5% as scale makes each $10B of volume worth less per share. House AFFO/share FY26E $4.41 -> FY30E $5.05 -> FY35E $5.77 (3.1% CAGR), roughly the FY2023-FY2026 cadence. Terminal 2.25% at a 9.5% cost of equity (14.1x AFFO exit); the 17x cap does not bind.

bull.narrative: Rate cuts take the 10-year back toward 4-4.5%: the equity re-rates, the cap-rate/cost-of-capital spread widens to 150bp+, and $10-12B/yr of volume at 7%+ yields becomes 4-5% per-share accretive again (the FY2018-FY2022 regime). The private-capital platform (Core Plus Fund $3.3B AUM, Apollo, KKR, GIC, Cloud Capital $6B) scales fee income to 3-4% of revenue at ~80% margins, lifting the AFFO margin ~120bp. Rent recapture stays above 100% and bad debt stays near 1%. House AFFO/share FY30E ~$5.43, FY35E ~$6.56; terminal 2.75% (15.2x exit, 19x cap not binding).

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 17x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: UNCHANGED from the 2026-10-02 build. Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% because the dominant valuation axis - the level of long rates - is outside management's control, O's growth model is wholly dependent on capital-markets access at an accretive multiple, leverage (5.4x) sits above MAA-type peers, and the retail book (73% of rent) carries live tenant-credit risk (Walgreens, dollar stores). Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs rate cuts, spread normalisation and fee-platform scaling to coincide. Not higher on bear: 32 years of unbroken dividend growth, AFFO/share has never fallen in the available history, occupancy 98.8% and rent recapture 103.5%. The November guidance raise and the KKR JV do not move the weights: the rate axis that drives them is essentially where it was (10-year 5.07% vs 5.24%).
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
